title: 1971 AHSME Problem 24
statement:
Pascal’s triangle is an array of positive integers, shown below, in which the first row is \(1,\) the second row is two \(1\)’s, each row begins and ends with \(1,\) and each other entry is the sum of the two entries above it.

The quotient of the number of entries in the first \(n\) rows which are not \(1\)’s and the number of \(1\)’s is:

solutions.text:
The first \(n\) rows contain \(1+2+\cdots+n=\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\) entries. There are \(2n-1\) boundary \(1\)’s, so the number of other entries is \[ \begin{gathered} \frac{n(n+1)}2-(2n-1)\\ =\frac{n^2+n-4n+2}{2}\\ =\frac{n^2-3n+2}{2}. \end{gathered} \] Dividing by \(2n-1\) gives \(\frac{n^2-3n+2}{4n-2}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Count all entries and then subtract the boundary \(1\)’s
The first \(n\) rows contain \(\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\) entries and \(2n-1\) boundary \(1\)’s
